rule_types.after: pedals: ids that must come BEFORE the rule's pedal
rule_types.before: pedals: ids that must come AFTER the rule's pedal
rule_types.after_group: group: a tag; the pedal must come after every pedal in the project with that tag
rule_types.before_group: group: a tag; the pedal must come before every pedal in the project with that tag
rule_types.no_buffered_before: no pedal with buffered_bypass=true may come earlier in the chain
rule_types.as_early_as_possible: sits right after the pedals its own 'after' rules require
rule_types.strength: 'required' fails validation if violated; 'preferred' only warns
rule_types.scope: rules listed on a catalog pedal are intrinsic (apply in every project); projects add their own in project.json and can disable or soften catalog rules by id via rule_overrides

pedals.name: Sun Face BC183

dependencies.reason: AnalogMan: the Fuzz Face must see the guitar directly; no buffered pedal ahead of it

pedals.comments: Silicon Fuzz Face, unbuffered: must be FIRST in the chain, guitar straight into it. Ships battery-only; check your unit has the optional DC jack. Silicon version is negative ground so sharing power is OK, but AnalogMan warns a supply can add hum/oscillation. 'Under 1 mA' is from the shared Fuzz Face page.

pedals.name: Beano Boost

dependencies.reason: AnalogMan: no buffered pedal ahead of the Beano

pedals.comments: Germanium treble booster, direct post-fuzz. Per AnalogMan it can share a DC supply with the Sun Face and other basic fuzzes (keep that group simple). The Oct 2020 manual text read by the research agent said isolated power only / no daisy-chaining, so confirm the wording for your unit. Never 9V AC. Needs the DC jack option (battery by default). Center-negative.

pedals.name: Double Dragon
pedals.comments: NOT in the current plan (the Danelectro 3699 is preferred); kept as an alternative. Lo-fi octave device (mono octave down + distorted octave up). 9V only: JHS warns damage above 9V. Silent buffered bypass (retailer-sourced; JHS page unreachable).

pedals.name: PolyTune 3
pedals.comments: Tuner / master front buffer. 100 mA is the manual's minimum supply rating; measured draw is lower (~38 mA reported for the Mini). Bypass mode is selectable by DIP switch (true by default, buffered, or buffered with display on); buffer ENABLED in this plan as the master front buffer. Has a power-out jack for daisy-chaining.

pedals.name: Mini Ego Compressor
pedals.comments: Compressor. Wampler publishes 14 mA at 9V and 22 mA at 18V (figure here is the 18V one). Page does not explicitly state the jack is 18V-rated. True bypass. Listed as 'Ego Mini' in the original plan.

pedals.name: Full-Drive 2 Mosfet
pedals.comments: Overdrive, more headroom at 18V. ~10 mA is from Fulltone's page for the newer v2; no manufacturer figure found for the original Mosfet model (one forum measurement: ~7 mA).

pedals.name: Phase 95
pedals.comments: Phaser, pre-dirt for a classic 70s sweep. No battery option. True bypass. Exempt from 'modulation after gain': intentionally ahead of the dirt.

pedals.name: Retrovibe
pedals.comments: Photocell Uni-Vibe, pre-dirt for throbbing fuzz-vibe tones. 120 mA assumes the current mk.4 (mk.3 is listed at 80-150 mA): check your version. True bypass, no battery. Exempt from 'modulation after gain': intentionally ahead of the dirt.

pedals.name: Red Muck Mk2
pedals.comments: Russian/Civil War Muff fuzz. Sources conflict: 60 mA (JAM shop page) vs 12-15 mA (retailers); planning on 60 mA until the manual is checked. True bypass.

pedals.name: Ratsbane
pedals.comments: Hard-clipping distortion. 2.5 mA at 9V, 3.2 mA at 18V; approved for 18V but designed around 9V. No battery connector. True bypass.

pedals.name: Protein V3
pedals.comments: Dual overdrive, placed post-Ratsbane to stack or smooth the hard clipping. 9V only ('18V is not better'). Fully analog (per owner), so it may share an output. True bypass (per owner; V3 uses soft/electronic switching per Browne). This is the V3. Browne's sources conflict for V3 current: manual says <100 mA, a Browne Q&A line says 130 mA, retailers quote ~30 mA. Planning on 130 mA (worst case).

pedals.name: Reticon Flanger
pedals.comments: Analog BBD flanger, post-dirt modulation. Needs an isolated 18V output, no battery. True bypass (per owner). 'Under 50 mA' is from search snippets of the PastFX page/manual (direct fetch failed): verify.

pedals.name: Analog Chorus
pedals.comments: Analog BBD chorus (M234). Buffered bypass per the Dunlop manual (one reviewer says it dulls highs when off). Battery or 9V DC.

pedals.name: Harmonious Monk Mk2
pedals.comments: Harmonic tremolo with digital tap controller. Analog signal path but a digital processor, so treated as DIGITAL: must not share an output. JAM recommends an isolated supply; 145 mA is JAM's max (third-party listings say 35-100 mA). True bypass.

pedals.name: Belle Epoch Deluxe
pedals.comments: Tape echo emulation. Analog EP-3-style circuitry around a 24-bit digital delay line, so treated as DIGITAL. Catalinbread lists 9V DC ONLY at 200 mA (it steps up to an internal rail itself): the original plan had it on 18V, which could damage it, so it is on a 9V output here. Give it a clean isolated output. Spelled 'Epoque' in the original plan.

pedals.name: Octahive
pedals.comments: High-octave fuzz. Planned for the practice board. 70 mA per a site you found (source not recorded, not a manufacturer figure; Effects Database lists the v2 as 9V DC center-negative with no mA). Check which version you own.

pedals.name: E-Lady
pedals.comments: Analog flanger (Mooer Electric Lady). Planned for the practice board. 10 mA per retailers, 9V DC center-negative, no battery (too small to fit one), true bypass.

pedals.name: Custom Shop Duke of Tone
pedals.playground_title: MXR Custom Shop Duke of Tone
pedals.comments: Overdrive (CSP039). Planned for the practice board. 6 mA at 9V, no battery option; Dunlop recommends the ECB003 or an MXR Brick. One retailer mentions 18V for extra headroom, not confirmed by Dunlop, so allowed at 9V only here.

pedals.name: Ditto Looper
pedals.comments: Looper. Planned for the practice board. 100 mA is the minimum supply rating (retailers/Rockboard), not a measured draw. 9V DC center-negative, no battery. One reviewer saw a nominal-9V supply output higher than 9V and kill it: use a regulated/isolated output.

pedals.name: 3699 Fuzz
pedals.comments: Fuzz/octaver, candidate to replace the JHS Double Dragon in the front fuzz group. 9 mA is from a single retailer listing (another says 3 mA; no Danelectro spec sheet found), so planning on 9 mA. Spec lists 9V DC, supply not included; a 9V battery is reported to work. Assumed 9V only. Planned for the gig board; placement after the Beano is a placeholder: confirm.

pedals.name: Carbon Copy
pedals.comments: Analog BBD delay (M169). 26 mA, 9V DC center-negative, true bypass (retailer specs; one UK retailer lists it as end of life). Planned for the practice board.

pedals.name: Flight Delay
pedals.comments: Delay with analog-style (BBD voiced) and DSP-style digital modes, so treated as DIGITAL (circuit not confirmed). Not in the plan yet (not in your Pedal Playground save, so marked not owned). 85 mA at 9V DC center-negative per retailers; JHS warns against going above 9V. Bypass type NOT FOUND (it has a Trails bypass mode, but no source says true vs buffered).

pedals.name: PolyTune 2
pedals.comments: Planned for the practice board. Full-size PolyTune 2 (not the Mini). About 45-50 mA per a retailer and TC's page for the original PolyTune (the PolyTune 2 manual spec was unreadable); the manual asks for a supply rated at least 100 mA. 9V DC center-negative, battery option, true bypass (no buffer; the PolyTune 3 adds one). Digital is inferred from the polyphonic display (no source says so explicitly).

pedals.name: Bass Big Muff Pi 2
pedals.comments: Planned for the bass board. 2026 small-enclosure reissue (not the original large Bass Big Muff Pi: that one draws 7 mA). ehx.com says 25 mA in the power section and 20 mA in the spec list (planning on 25); 9V DC center-negative, do not exceed 12V; battery included. Analog circuit, true bypass via mechanical relay.

pedals.name: SansAmp VT Bass DI
pedals.comments: Planned for the bass board. Preamp / stompbox / XLR DI. About 6 mA at 9V DC center-negative (100 mA minimum supply rating per the manual); also runs on 9V battery or 24-48V phantom power. 100% analog. Not true bypass: with the SansAmp circuit off it acts as an active transparent direct box, so the input buffer and XLR driver stay active (the manual does not call it 'buffered' explicitly).

pedals.name: Hyper Luminal
pedals.comments: Planned for the bass board. Analog VCA audio path controlled by a digital side-chain (time constants editable via the Darkglass Suite), so treated as DIGITAL: must not share an output. 250 mA at 9V DC center-negative, REGULATED supply only (unregulated or higher voltage can cause noise/damage); no battery option listed. Bypass type NOT FOUND: manufacturer silent, retailers conflict (buffered / true bypass / 'no'). Reported discontinued or out of stock at several retailers.

pedals.name: Tumnus Deluxe
pedals.comments: Klon-style EQ/overdrive: dead last, master mid-stack and buffer. Runs at 9V ONLY (boosts the rail internally, do not use 18V). Buffered or true bypass via side switch (buffer enabled in this plan). 70.3 mA at 9V. Deliberately not tagged 'gain' so the 'modulation after gain' rules do not apply to it.
